描述_ZN: The Wisteria Scroll, Modern, painted by Chen Shizeng, on paper with color, 137 cm in length and 32.7 cm in width.　　The upper right side of this panel is self-titled: "Elegantly corrected by Mr. Xiu Kang Ren. Chen Hengke of Xiushui in the summer of Kuaihai." Inscribed with the seal of "rotten".　　The year "Kuihai" refers to the twelfth year of the Republic of China (1923).　　This picture belongs to the painting method of "red flowers and ink leaves". The vine is a common garden plant in traditional Chinese houses. It has both dense flowers and leaves for people to enjoy and thick shade for people to keep cool. When the flowers are in bloom, bunches of lavender flowers dangle from the leaves, with a pale color and a pleasant fragrance. The most distinctive feature of Chen Shizeng's Wisteria is his composition. Paintings usually highlight the drooping nature of the vine, so the flowering branches are often placed at the top of the painting, with the lower part of the painting empty. Chen Shizeng does the opposite, concentrating on the lower part of the composition and echoing the upper part with a few flowering branches to achieve a balanced picture. The staccato and powerful brushwork shows the vigor and robustness of the old vine.
